So I'll stop there, and I think we're going to be going into questions, and we'll be happy to answer as many of those as we can.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question is from Jeremy Pearlman with Maxim Group.

Jeremy Pearlman: Firstly, you mentioned that you're finalizing the U.S. pivotal study design, probably hopefully within this quarter. Is there any information you could share, maybe more details regarding what that study size might look like? What are some of the primary, secondary endpoints, and the expected enrollment duration?

Richard Ferrari: Yes, this is Rich. I'll give you some points to that, and Branislav, maybe you want to end with a couple of points. But I can tell you that we haven't arrived yet with agreement on the size of the trial, but we've had very, very good conversations with the FDA, and we have a proposal to the FDA based on a statistical model from Harvard University. And I would again give you the range that we think is most likely, probably in around 300 patient size for the trial. So when you think about that, we'll have approximately 8 centers, possibly 10 centers enrolling.

If you took a very, very conservative approach to enrollment, now remember, these are the top cardiac centers in the country, but let's just use a conservative number that they enroll 10 patients a month. If it were 8 centers, let's just use 10 centers and make it a lot easier, that would be 100 patients enrolled in the trial every single month. Three months, you'd be at 300 patients. So that's a rough estimate. Now, it may take us 4 months to enroll, or what have you, but the fact of the matter is, every other trial that we have, in fact, started, enrolled faster than what we thought. So we do have, I think, a high confidence level.

Our centers are excited. As Branislav had mentioned, the ALIGN-ACS basically is the proxy, if you will, for the pivotal trial. So we're quite confident that we will get approval from the FDA. And like I said, it's a question of whether or not that happens before year-end or at the very beginning of 2027.

Branislav Vajdic: Yes, I would like to just supplement this. We have a proposal to the FDA now through this Breakthrough program that is going to result in a quite timely feedback. And it is, at this point, a very solid proposal. We believe it addresses all the concerns. But at this point, we cannot be sure really what the FDA reaction will be, inasmuch as we feel very good about what we are proposing to the FDA. So things may change a bit from what Rich has described, but we are very confident of the material that we are submitting.

Richard Ferrari: Yes. You had also asked about the secondary endpoints, and I don't know that we've completely defined those yet as we're having these conversations, but we will in the final package.

Jeremy Pearlman: Right. No, I understand. I understand it's still early, it hasn't been finalized, but I appreciate all that extra information. Maybe just segueing from that, the FDA regulatory pathway, what -- again, this also might be a little too early, but what clinical evidence and performance thresholds do you think would be required from the FDA to get clearance, that 510(k) clearance?

Richard Ferrari: Branislav, go ahead and touch on that.

Branislav Vajdic: Yes. ALIGN-ACS study that we just presented at TCT conference is sort of mirroring the endpoints that we propose now to the FDA, right? And I described our results, and really those results that you have seen in my slide there, there will be endpoints that we propose. And again, performance that we have seen in this pilot study is very encouraging indeed. And the pivotal study, it could be viewed as an enlarged same design that we have tested now already in this pilot study called ALIGN-ACS.

Jeremy Pearlman: Okay. Understood. And then this may be the last question from me. Are there -- I know you do have existing FDA clearance for arrhythmia detection. Are there any -- and I know it's clear that the focus is on heart attack detection, and I understand that, but are there any opportunities to maybe monetize that already clearance, maybe through licensing, a strategic partnership where you wouldn't have to put in a lot of capital or resources behind it, but still be able to monetize it in some way?

Richard Ferrari: Well, I think it's a great question. Our focus, as you've heard us say before, with the arrhythmia detection right now, monetizing it in a large way is -- just simply isn't the focus. But we are, quite frankly, again, working with, as we mentioned before, a number of powerful concierge practices. They are putting units into the hands of patients. It's just not a significant event at the moment, or as a learning and understanding of the use parameters.

Now we've also had, as you might imagine, since the ALIGN-ACS data, we have had a number of folks who are interested in what it is we're doing, and the technology may be able to be utilized in something they may be doing. But it's really too early to say. We're clearly open to those kinds of discussions. But at the moment, I think revenue generated from commercialization is just being modest, and we're testing the market and trying to understand reimbursement and trying to understand the use parameters and understanding how physicians will, let's call it, prescribe our product to their patients.

Operator: Our next question is from Yi Chen with H.C. Wainwright.

Ahmed Mahmoud: This is Ahmed on for Yi. So for suspected heart attacks, what response time would the reader service need to deliver? And who would be responsible for urgent escalation? And how would you handle a patient with ongoing symptoms whose tracing is negative or inconclusive?

Richard Ferrari: Yes, I'm going to let Branislav answer.

Branislav Vajdic: Sure. Absolutely. Our current, I would say, conversations with our reader service indicate that they would be quite comfortable with 30-minute commitment. Perhaps we will end up with 15-minute reaction time commitment. We are in the middle of those negotiations with them. And that will be a 24/7 indeed. And it is all about accelerating time to intervention, which is, again, critical parameter basically determining the outcome for that patient. As far as those patients that appear to be normal in terms of there is no ECG change and the symptoms may not be suggesting a heart attack, we are fully aware that without blood draw and troponin level, we cannot rule out, nobody can rule out a heart attack.

So, those patients will be told the truth, which is, "We don't have enough information to tell you anything about your condition, right?" And if you feel this is a life-threatening situation, call 911, right? So, that's the standard of care right now, right? So if we don't have enough information, we don't have blood draw, then we're going to just tell them the standard of care applies.

Ahmed Mahmoud: I guess, one quick question on strategy for the launch. So, from the initial arrhythmia launch, anything that you learned about the patient willingness to adopt the device or -- and their willingness to pay? And how -- I guess, where do you interpret those lessons to adjust your commercial approach for heart attack assessment?

Richard Ferrari: Well, remember, the first step into that understanding is working with the concierge practices, right? Those practices that have a good body of patients that would be considered at-risk cardiac patients. So, that particular model that we have been exploring was where the service themselves would acquire the product from us and provide it then to those patients as part of "the concierge fee." And we're -- and they have been doing that. And we -- I can't say that we've 100% have solidified exactly how that model long-term will work. But for right now, that's what they are doing.

So, the concierge service buys from us, then they provide that to those patients that they think would benefit from it. And it's, again, I think a win-win. From the patient's point of view, obviously, they're quite ecstatic to have a device that would enable them to, in a sense, get comfort from the fact that it may be 2:00 in the morning, it may be some other hour of the day in which they're feeling something strange, that they have an ability to actually take a reading and understand whether or not they should do something more.

Now long-term, once we get -- for the MI detection done, I think that whole approach is going to take on a completely different look. Because now you've got a device that would, in fact, notify someone if they're having a heart attack. And for those patients that falls into that category, which, as you know, is some 20 million of kind of what we would call acute and severe cardiac concern, we're testing how much they would pay for a subscription as we're working with our reimbursement people and what CMS and/or payers would pay.

But the significance of having a device, the first handheld device to be able to determine whether or not you're having an MI or not, has been received in every situation that we've ever presented it in, to every single physician that we've ever presented it to, with an overwhelming response to, "I got to have this. When are you guys going to have the full approval?" So, we're confident that between now and, let's call it this time next year, we'll have that very, very well mapped out and understood.

Unknown Executive: Our first webcast question asks, "With the December 28th NASDAQ minimum bid compliance deadline approaching, can management provide an update on the strategy to regain compliance? And is the company considering or requesting an extension or evaluating alternative measures to maintain its NASDAQ listing? Or will there be any catalyst events within the next 7 months?

Timothy Cruickshank: Yes. Great. Thank you. Yes, we're in communication with NASDAQ and in good standing. So at this point, we're fully expecting an extension, which would be another 180 days. And if you look at what was presented today in terms of things we know about with the clinical study, enrollment times, and some heart attack detection catalysts, in addition to potential partnerships or other things that are working behind the scenes, we fully believe we're working towards organically rectifying this, and that's the approach the company's taking at this point. So we remain very confident in our ability to regain compliance organically.

And we'll obviously need to take all considerations should the time come, but we're not expecting it at this point.

Unknown Executive: Our next and last webcast question asks, "Have there been any ongoing discussions in the matter of partnerships?" Realizing that Singapore seems to be one potential partner, I think they may mean Indonesia.

Richard Ferrari: Once again, there hasn't been "formal discussions." There have been some inputs. And regarding Indonesia, we're going to wait and see what comes from the full data set when it's fully analyzed. We do know that they have a very high interest in what HeartBeam has offered. I can't say that's going to lead to any licensing or investment at this time, but what I can tell you is, they enrolled these patients in record time. It's actually quite important to their health care system, and we have very high-level connections with the Ministry of Health there. Regarding at least 2 other companies where one might consider, could there be a partnership of some sort?

Too early in the conversations to be able to make any real predictive statement about.

Operator: We have reached the end of our question-and-answer session. I would like to turn the call over back to Mr. Ferrari for closing remarks.

Richard Ferrari: Well, again, thank you for those questions. I know those are the important pieces of information to understanding HeartBeam. But again, I just reemphasize that if you look at the size of the market that we have available to us, the sheer importance of our technology, which has already been proven, the impact that we believe it's going to make, not only to the health care system, but clearly to many, many patients' lives, the fact that we view this as extremely low risk and pure execution on our part, we're very, very confident in what we're doing moving forward.

And I think our next quarter, when we have this particular call, you're going to see further evidence of all of those statements that I just made. We'll have further clarity from the FDA, and on the other initiatives that we're working on. But again, this is just pure execution from the HeartBeam team, and we're grateful to be in that position, actually. So thank you again for all of your interest, and we appreciate the time today.

Operator: This concludes today's teleconference. You may disconnect your lines at this time. Thank you for your participation.

#3070. Newsmax (NMAX) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Affiliate growth and AI licensing deals fueled results, with a one-time fee adding a notable lift.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Newsmax Inc. (NMAX -5.81%) reported record quarterly revenue driven by structural growth in affiliate fees and international licensing, alongside a $14.0 million nonrecurring fee from an advertising agreement amendment. Management stated that the company is shifting its focus toward high-margin digital streams and AI content partnerships while reducing investment in legacy print and newsletter products. The company reported that the midterm election cycle serves as a precursor to the 2028 presidential cycle, which is expected to drive higher national advertising and audience engagement beginning in 2027.

Operator: Good afternoon, and welcome to the Newsmax Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. [Operator Instructions] It is now my pleasure to turn the floor over to your host, Chris Odeh, Investor Relations. The floor is yours.

Chris O'Day: Good afternoon, and welcome to Newsmax's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. I'm joined today by Chris Ruddy, Chief Executive Officer; and Darryle Burnham, Chief Financial Officer. On this call, Chris and Darryle will provide prepared remarks on the most recent quarter. We will then take questions from the investment community. A recording of this conference call will be available on our Investor Relations website shortly after the call has ended. Please note that this call may include forward-looking statements regarding Newsmax's financial performance and operating results. These statements are based on management's current expectations. Actual results could differ from what is stated due to certain factors identified on today's call and in the company's SEC filings.

Additionally, this call will include certain non-GAAP financial measures. Reconciliations of these measures are included in the earnings release and our SEC filings, which are available in the Investor Relations section of our website. I will now turn the call over to Chris Ruddy, Chief Executive Officer of Newsmax. Chris?

Christopher Ruddy: Thank you, Chris, and welcome, everyone, to our third quarter 2026 earnings call. The third quarter was the strongest in our history as a public company. Excluding a one-time payment, which Darryle will cover in detail, revenue grew 21.6% to a record $55 million, and adjusted EBITDA was $5 million. That is our highest quarterly revenue and our fastest growth rate since our listing, and it was our second consecutive adjusted EBITDA positive quarter. The quality of our growth was on full display relative to the overall cycle. We are at the midpoint of the presidential election cycle when cable news audiences and national advertising demand are generally well below their peak.

Even in that environment, affiliate fees and licensing, 2 areas we expected to carry our growth this year, did exactly that. Affiliate agreements are renewing at higher rates. Licensing is taking the Newsmax brand globally and on leading AI platforms as news consumption diversifies. In every one of these markets, there is real demand for independent common-sense journalism, and we are positioned to deliver it. Affiliate fees rose 77% to $14.3 million. Newsmax is a relatively new entrant to affiliate fees. As our agreements come up for renewal, they are repricing at rates that reflect our reach and ratings today. These are multiyear agreements, so each renewal sets a higher base for the years ahead.

In addition to renewals, we continued to gain traction in the quarter. We added 6 new Newsmax affiliates, each as an independent cable operator. These are smaller agreements, but each one increases our reach. Even as viewing shifts across platforms, linear news still has a strong place. We are well positioned to keep that presence, and it introduces viewers to everything else we offer. We also launched on AFN, the streaming service of the American Forces Network, bringing Newsmax to service members and their families stationed overseas. We also agreed to acquire 2 radio stations in Miami, adding a historic South Florida broadcast brand to the places where people can find Newsmax.

Our second growth engine is brand and international licensing, our fastest-growing revenue stream. Licensing revenue was up 343% year-over-year as the agreements we expanded earlier this year flowed through our results. We are on track for approximately $16 million in international licensing fees this year, all of it under agreements already signed, and we estimate annualized licensing revenues of approximately $25 million next year. Our footprint is also growing. Newsmax Ukraine launched on November 1. And in October, we were pleased to receive the special recognition award from the Royal Television Society in the U.K. for our role in helping our partners build out the Newsmax Ukraine Studios during wartime.

Our licensing partners are also preparing Newsmax for additional countries in Europe. We will have additional details for our shareholders in the future. We are also proud to announce that Newsmax is now available on all major pay TV platforms in Israel, and Newsmax en Español is now on 3 streaming distributors in the United States with more to come. These are true partnerships built in a capital-efficient way and serving underserved audiences around the world. Advertising held up well. Cable advertising revenue grew 3% year-over-year in a soft market. It has consistently run ahead of what our ratings alone would suggest because advertisers value a loyal and engaged audience that watches news live. Our audience is the reason.

The 2024 election brought millions of new viewers to Newsmax, and they have stayed with us. Through the first 9 months of this year, we reached nearly 49 million viewers, in line with the same period of the 2024 election and up 42% from 2023. We are the fourth-highest-rated cable news channel, ranked #2 in the category for engagement among adults 35 to 64 and remain the fastest-growing basic cable network since Nielsen began measuring us in 2020. Our viewers are highly engaged, spending an average of 25 minutes per tune in, up from 14 minutes in 2020. They are also loyal.

3.3 million of them watch Newsmax without tuning into any of the 3 largest cable news networks, including Fox News. When the news cycle slows, our viewers do not leave. Each election brings new viewers to Newsmax, and they keep watching us, so our audience builds from one cycle to the next. The way people find news is not standing still, and neither are we. News consumption is diversifying across cable, OTT streaming, social and now AI. Newsmax is on all platforms for all people. Our social total followers rose 13% year-over-year to 26.8 million at the end of the quarter, and our followers are highly engaged.

We generated 44 million interactions in the third quarter, up 4% from the second quarter on less content. And on Facebook, we ranked first among news publishers in interactions per follower. Newsmax2, our free streaming channel, is carried on almost all the major free streaming platforms. Today, N2 broadcasts over the air on digital channels in 131 markets, reaching approximately 87% of U.S. TV households. As our presence grows, so does our ability to monetize it, and we are taking more control of the advertising opportunity on N2, Newsmax2, in the quarters to come. Turning to Newsmax+, our paid streaming platform, we are seeing high engagement.

We have also grown our online news sharing with Yahoo News, MSN, SmartNews, Apple, and Google. We see AI as having a particularly strong potential benefit in terms of reach and revenues, and I hope to see some developments in the coming year. And the cycle is turning. As a reminder, advertising for midterm races for Congress and state and local elections primarily goes towards local broadcast stations, local cable and pay TV operators, and local digital. Newsmax is a national cable news network, so a relatively small amount of that spending comes our way. What we gain is engagement and new viewers. This was a heated midterm race.

And as we saw after 2024, the viewers it brings to Newsmax tend to remain with us. It is also a precursor of what is to come. Political ad spending for these midterms was projected at $11.6 billion, according to AdImpact, more than the total spend in the 2024 presidential cycle. Looking ahead to 2028, we believe the presidential race, coupled with federal and state races, will only amplify the money spent. Newsmax expects to benefit more in terms of advertising during the 2028 cycle. The presidential race begins in earnest in 2027 with the first primary debates expected to take place in the summer of 2027.

It is an open race for the White House with no incumbent and an expected crowded field in both parties. Our cable channel, Newsmax, reached 58 million total viewers in 2025 with no national election, and we have only widened our presence across platforms since. We intend to build on that in the year ahead as the 2028 presidential election heats up, providing a trusted outlet for the underserved independent and center-right market. Looking ahead, we continue to expect our growth to be structural, not cyclical, led by affiliate fee expansion and international licensing. Darryle will walk through our full year outlook in his remarks. Let me close, as I always do, with the big picture.

Few media companies can reach this audience with the scale, credibility and multi-platform presence of Newsmax. We see a 2-year window into the 2028 cycle, and we are entering it from a position of strength. Record revenue, a second consecutive profitable quarter, a loyal audience across cable, streaming and digital -- we are excited about the journey ahead, and we will continue to invest behind growth. To our readers, our viewers, our advertisers and our shareholders, thank you. With that, I will turn it over to our Chief Financial Officer, Darryle Burnham, to walk through the financials. Darryle?

Darryle Burnham: Thank you, Chris, and thank you, everyone, for joining us today. As Chris highlighted, we delivered record underlying revenues and our second consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA. Before getting into the numbers, we want to touch on 2 items that affect how this quarter reads. First, the one-time item Chris mentioned. During the third quarter, we recognized $14 million in connection with an amendment to an advertising purchase agreement with a customer, which modified the parties' remaining rights and obligations. The amount is nonrecurring. It is presented as a new service revenue termination fee line within our Broadcast segment. So our advertising revenue does not include it.

Where it matters, we will give our results both with and without it. Second, our digital segment now includes a licensing line for the first time, reflecting $0.6 million of revenue from our media and AI content agreements. We expect content deals and other partnerships with AI companies to grow over the coming years. Setting the one-time item aside, the quarter shows the same shift we described last quarter. Our revenue mix continued to move toward higher-margin, concentrated affiliate fee and licensing revenues, and higher rates across both expanded gross margin. Gross margin was 55.3% in the third quarter or 44%, excluding the one-time item, compared to 35.3% in the prior year quarter.

We will continue to invest behind this growth. Our capital allocation priorities remain focused on supporting long-term growth, which include investment in programming, talent, technology, distribution, digital initiatives and other strategic opportunities. Turning to our third quarter results. In the third quarter, we delivered $69 million in total revenues, representing a 52.5% increase year-over-year. Excluding the $14 million one-time item, total revenues were a record $55 million, an increase of 21.6% year-over-year. Breaking this down by revenue stream for the quarter, starting with our reportable segments. Total broadcasting revenues grew 65.9% year-over-year to $60.7 million in the third quarter of 2026, which includes the $14 million one-time item. Without it, broadcasting revenues grew 27.6% to $46.7 million.

Our growth in broadcasting was driven by higher affiliate fee revenue attributed to new contractual relationships and rate increases that took effect in late 2025 and '26 and by expanded international licensing agreements. Total digital revenues decreased 4.1% year-over-year to $8.3 million in the third quarter of 2026. The new media and AI licensing revenue was more than offset by lower subscription revenue, product sales and digital advertising. Now turning to our revenue by component. Advertising revenues were $28.1 million, a 1.9% year-over-year increase as higher cable and satellite advertising from midterm election-related demand was partially offset by lower digital advertising.

Affiliate revenues increased 77.4% year-over-year to $14.3 million, driven by new contractual relationships as well as rate increases that took effect in late 2025 and 2026. Subscription revenues of $6.1 million were down 12% year-over-year due to lower new customer acquisition, partially offset by gains from expanded affiliate agreements that make Newsmax available on more linear cable providers. Product sales revenues decreased 21.2% year-over-year to $1.2 million, primarily reflecting lower book and supplement sales. Licensing revenues were $5.4 million, up $1.2 million in the prior year quarter, supported by the amended international licensing agreement and revenue from our media and AI content agreements.

We reported quarterly net income of $15.2 million, or $0.12 per share, compared to a net loss of $4.1 million, or $0.03 per share, in the prior year quarter. The improvement was primarily driven by higher total revenue, growth in high-margin affiliate fee and licensing revenue and lower legal expenses, partially offset by continued investment in programming and production. Our quarterly adjusted EBITDA was $19 million, an improvement of $20 million from the negative $0.9 million reported in the same quarter last year. Excluding the one-time item, adjusted EBITDA was $5 million, positive for the second consecutive quarter.

The underlying improvement was primarily due to growth in high-margin affiliate fee and licensing revenue, partially offset by continued investment in programming, production and OTT initiatives. We ended the quarter with $26.7 million in cash and cash equivalents and $110.8 million in short-term investments, bringing our total cash and investment position to $137.6 million with no debt on the balance sheet. Turning to our outlook. We are maintaining our underlying full year 2026 revenue guidance of $212 million to $216 million. That represents 13% growth year-over-year at the midpoint of the range. Including the one-time item, our full year 2026 revenue guidance is $226 million to $230 million.

We are encouraged by our performance through the first 9 months of the year and remain confident as we look ahead. Our higher-margin affiliate fee and licensing streams are the biggest levers for margin improvement in the near term. At the same time, as we continue to scale the business, reduce our legacy spend and focus on opportunities to improve margins through revenue growth from content investment, technology, and monetization across multiple platforms. In closing, we remain focused on disciplined execution as we continue to invest in content, distribution and OTT initiatives that support long-term growth.

With a strong balance sheet, no debt and a diversified multi-platform revenue model, we believe we are well positioned to deliver sustainable value for our shareholders. Thank you for your time today. Now we would like to open the line for analyst questions. Operator?

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Thomas Forte from Maxim.

Thomas Forte: Great. So first off, Chris and Darryle, congratulations on the strong quarter. I have one question and one follow-up. I'll go one at a time. Chris, you gave some very thoughtful comments in your prepared remarks, and I was hoping you could go through them one more time as far as the engagement and monetization for Newsmax typically when you compare the midterms with the presidential election?

Christopher Ruddy: Tom, thank you for that. Darryle, our CFO, has done studies and reviewed previous presidential election cycles. And invariably, as far back as we can find, the 2 years leading up before a presidential election usually leads to much higher engagement revenues and benefits the company generally overall. Sometimes we call it the Super Bowl of elections. And it's already clearly started in earnest. Just look at headlines across the web today about Rubio and Vance -- and so all of that attracts attention, a lot of drama, a lot of political interest. And I think that will help grow. At the same time, you have a divided Congress. That is going to play very significantly.

There'll be a lot of heavy fundraising and political developments as related to that. We expect to benefit. As engagement grows, ratings grow and all our different platforms tend to see increases, that should be good for overall revenues.

Thomas Forte: Excellent. And then for my follow-up, it sounds like you acquired 2 radio stations in Miami. Can you remind investors what your strategy is when it comes to M&A? And then looking ahead, what types of assets would you consider acquiring versus building on your own?

Christopher Ruddy: Newsmax has always had an interest in radio. We come out of the radio ecosphere in the sense that a lot of radio hosts have promoted Newsmax through the years from the days we started as a dot-com in the '90s. I think we were probably the most aligned with radio talk show hosts in the country. That market is huge. On any given month, there are 30 million to 50 million people tuning into talk radio according to various industry estimates. In some ways, it's believed to be bigger than the cable news market. And they are very highly engaged and passionate people. Over the years, radio is considered legacy media.

The numbers have gone down on radio, but podcasts, which are quite related to radio, have gone up. And if you see some of the most successful podcasters, there are also people that are on radio or have radio affiliations. Newsmax got involved in radio with a syndicated radio show we launched several years ago, The Rob Carson Show, which is a talk radio show that broadcasts from 12 to 2 every day. It's in about 35 markets, I believe, right now. We have this opportunity for a Spanish-speaking station in Miami, it's very famous, Radio Mambí, and a sister station the company there owned. And the company that owned it had not been investing in the programming.

It had lost some of its audience, but the name is excellent. The reach of the signal on both stations is good. It reaches pretty much the Miami-Dade marketplace, which is a burgeoning market. We have not been involved in the Latino community much with any business. We thought this would be a good toehold for us to not only be in radio, but to also get a foothold in the Spanish-speaking market where we could start by producing social media and other podcasting content using that radio station as a base. So we thought it was a good step. I'm not sure I would describe it as part of a larger merger and acquisition strategy that we have.

We're certainly open to ideas, but we like continuing to grow our platforms where they are now, which is in cable, streaming, the Plus service we have and our app, and we're doing those as well as ancillary things like social media.

Operator: Next question comes from Michael Kupinski from Noble Capital Markets.

There does seem to be a significant increase certainly in -- we mentioned in one of our statements today that there is an increased engagement in viewing time of people spending on the app year-over-year. And that's being helped. We're doing not only news, not only documentaries, we're doing some scripted TV shows from the '60s and '70s, programs like Bonanza, Dragnet. We'll be adding more of those -- we're doing some movies. We have a very big genre in a third channel we added called World at War, our military history channel. And we have been adding recently a lot of true crime or police body cam, police live-to-tape series to Newsmax. One is called Caught on Bodycam.

We just bought Bad Hombres, which was a program that was developed documentary series for the ICE during their recent operations. That just premiered on Newsmax, will be part of the app. So we think in those genres, there'll be a lot of interest. But we see ourselves as a family-friendly news and entertainment app. And in the long run, we think there'll be a big market for that because we don't think the current app services, Netflix, Paramount, Disney, are focusing on that audience. And so it gives us a niche to move into while allowing for broad distribution of the channels, Newsmax 1 and Newsmax2.

Jacob Mutchler: Got you. Great. And then if you could also just talk about how extensively AI is being used internally today in content creation and in production? And just how much additional opportunity do you see to improve efficiency and reduce costs with AI internally?

Christopher Ruddy: I would say that it's being used in almost every department of the company. And there's good reason to use it, whether it's in the marketing department developing promotional materials, whether it's in accounting developing presentation materials or verifying or researching or double-checking data on our legal section, it's been a great help. We go and double-check legal documents with it. We don't see it as substituting a lot of things, but we see it improves productivity, efficiency and also provides verification on a lot of things. I know in the TV wing in terms of producing shows, not only are they using it to help developing the content of the program, but graphics, visuals where appropriate.

And then the website, it's speeding up the amount of articles being written. We don't generally do an article just based on AI. It's -- but the AI could be forming part of the background information. And where an article might have taken 2 or 3 hours to put together and post on the web, it might take less than an hour now or even sooner. So these are very dramatic effects. Sometimes they're more difficult to quantify, but I do think that will impact the number of employees we need as we grow.

Jacob Mutchler: Congratulations on a solid quarter.

Operator: Your next question comes from Nick McKay from Freedom Capital.

Nick McKay: Can you speak to the importance of the digital segment in the years ahead, especially given the history of revenue declines and negative adjusted EBITDA? Is there a world where divesting the digital segment makes sense and focusing more on broadcasting given more favorable economics?

Christopher Ruddy: Darryle, would you like to chat about that?

Darryle Burnham: Sure. Well, thank you. I think that the digital segment is key strategically to the overall growth of the company. It has been something that, as Chris mentioned, we haven't put a lot of focus on recently, but it is really the basis for the growth of the company over our 28-year history. I think one of the advantages that we have in the digital segment when you compare us to a Fox and a CNN is that we've built that relationship with the customer.

I think that the digital segment is key to participate in that growth and continue to be a very strategic component of the company overall.

Christopher Ruddy: Yes. I mean, our approach, we started as a digital media company and continue to be very strong. But as Darryle well explained that, that has been a tremendous tool for us to communicate to grow TV audience, to grow app audience, to grow social media -- some people just see it as a -- in terms of economics on the numbers, but they're missing the fact that it's actually growing other parts of the company, and it's more of a base from which we launch things and communicate directly. I think we started as we're the only digital website company that went into cable and launched and has had a successful cable channel that I know of.

The only one. Vice went in and they had a channel free that they basically licensed their name with, I think it's with A&E. But they didn't -- they're not truly -- in fact, it's been, I think, separate companies. We actually, organically from the web, started cable channel and have been very successful. And we always say that the digital side was the key growth factor. And then the amount of distribution, we're seeing just tremendous growth of the reach because our brand is becoming more and more powerful, not only internationally, right?

We see that, but across the ecosphere of digital world, our content is now widely picked up by MSN, Yahoo, Google News, Apple, SmartNews in that we have agreements with some of these as well to move our content, and we hope to increase even more. And we did a deal with Meta, and they're using our content from the digital side in the AI world, which we've released that and made that announcement. So there'll be lots of benefits from the digital. So don't -- if you see the newsletters, for instance, contracting, that is more of our plan -- part of a larger company strategic plan rather than something that's happening that's a negative thing for the company.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] We have no further questions on the lines. Thank you. This does conclude today's conference call. You may disconnect your phone lines at this time, and have a wonderful day. Thank you for your participation.

AI-powered data analytics provider Palantir Technologies is this week's first pick. The company reported market-beating second-quarter results. Moreover, Palantir raised its full-year guidance and now expects U.S. commercial business revenue to grow by at least 134%.

Following the Q2 print, Bank of America analyst Mariana Perez Mora reiterated a buy rating on PLTR stock with a price target of $255. Amazon's backlog gained from robust demand across both core workloads and AI adoption. Anmuth also observed the strength in AWS' AI and chips businesses, Graviton revenue commitments, and AWS' core business.

#3066. What's the Value of a Founder? Nvidia Offers the Greatest Test Yet

Jensen Huang's departure revives a longstanding investor debate of the value of a founder. Can Nvidia deliver without him?

In Wall Street and Silicon Valley, the debate over the difference between founder and non-founder-led companies has long raged.

According to research from Bain & Co., founder-led companies outperformed non-founder-led by 2.1x over a period from 2015 to 2025, generating a shareholder return of 443% compared 215% for non-founder-led companies.

In the tech sector, the difference was even starker with founder-led tech companies beating their tech peers by 2.6x.

That question is especially relevant following the exit of Nvidia's (NVDA -4.34%) Jensen Huang, who was embroiled in a scandal that began with his admission that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

Some commentators have noted that several other big tech companies have lost their founder CEOs and continued to perform well. Notably, Tim Cook ably took the reins from Steve Jobs, and Amazon has continued its strong growth under Andy Jassy.

However, those situations are considerably different than the one facing Nvidia. The AI chip titan had no succession plan in place, and Huang ran the company with an unusually high degree of control with approximately 60 direct reports. The board was not expecting to make such a decision, and employees were shocked by the sudden move. Some have circulated a petition calling for Huang's return, and at Nvidia headquarters, there were flowers laid by the entrance and video of a woman crying.

A number of Huang's fellow founders have weighed in on the move, criticizing the board's decision. Shopify's Tobi Lütke called it a generational blunder, adding, "There's no replacing a founder like Jensen," and that the new company would be a thing cosplaying as Nvidia. Elon Musk affirmed another post saying, "You do not simply replace the founder," while Binance's Changpeng Zhao said it was a mistake for the board to let Huang resign.

Founders likely have their own biases toward founder-led companies, but they're also intimately familiar with the characteristics that separate founder-led companies from the rest.

CFO Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO, and speculation has already built about who will become permanent CEO. The board is considering both internal and external candidates, and early frontrunners for the job include Ian Buck, the Vice President and General Manager of Hyperscale and High-Performance Computing (HPC) at Nvidia. Buck built CUDA, the software platform that's central to the company's industry dominance. Apple's chief hardware officer, Johny Srouji, is also reportedly being considered as a permanent CEO.

Nvidia's book of business for the next year or two is mostly set, but the real test for the next CEO will be over the next three to five years from now, which will be greatly influenced by the planning and strategy it sets now.

Even before Huang's job appeared to be in jeopardy, Nvidia stock looked undervalued. The stock had slumped through much of October and early November on fears that rising interest rates could pressure the AI Infrastructure build-out and then on fears that Democrats could crack down on data centers following the midterm elections.

Currently, Nvidia is expected to generate $15.93 in adjusted earnings per share next year, meaning it trades at less than 11 times forward earnings. That looks remarkably cheap for a company with Nvidia's competitive advantages and that's expected to grow revenue 68% next year.

Of course, the stock just became significantly riskier, but the valuation helps provide a floor on the stock that it wouldn't otherwise have.

There are a lot of variables at play here, including the outcome of any federal investigations on the company and Huang. Investors will gradually get some answers as to what to expect from Nvidia in the coming quarters and years.

However, this also might be the most definitive test yet for the value of a founder. If Nvidia continues to thrive, that will be a testament to the company that Huang built, even if it means he was ultimately replaceable.

Today, we will cover our third quarter results and highlights. Update you on our 3 strategic priorities I laid out at Investor Day, and share where we are focused heading into 2027.

CARFAX crossed 3 significant milestones in the quarter. 100 thousand service shops contributing data, 40 billion CARFAX vehicle history records, and 60 million consumers who have registered for CarCare. We continue to build our strategic assets for the future. In a dynamic automotive market, the scale of our data advantage and consumer reach is more valuable than ever. In CARFAX US, the go to market adjustments we made in June are working. The sales improvement we saw late in the second quarter carried through the third. With broad based momentum across our dealer products.

We are building on that progress with better tools and additional talent across our commercial organization. Outside the U.S, the Canada team is executing well in a tough market. And in Europe, we are pleased with the early results of our launch in Germany. Turning to B2B. We had a solid quarter despite market pressure on OEMs and suppliers. In Sales Solutions, we continue to evolve our product suite and acquire new customers. We had a significant win in the quarter as a large global OEM chose us for the breadth of what Mobility Global can offer. With CARFAX products being a differentiator. This shows the power of what 1 Mobility Global can make possible.

I will start with AI. Where I am spending much of my time. As the market adopts AI, its use for productivity and efficiency is becoming table stakes. Our opportunity goes further. Applying AI to Mobility Global's unique combination of assets: our industry-leading proprietary data, trusted brands, an industry wide customer network and products embedded in customers' everyday decisions. AI helps us unlock value from our assets faster than ever before. Our AI advantage starts with proprietary data. Over decades, we have built a data estate spanning more than 180 thousand sources that is extremely difficult to replicate. As AI reshapes how decisions are made, we believe trusted decision grade data becomes increasingly valuable.

And AI allows us to extract more value from that data than ever before. We are currently seeing this creating opportunities in 2 areas. Accelerating innovation across our products and expanding how consumers engage with our information. First, innovation. Where our data sets us apart. AI is transforming how we efficiently we acquire, interpret and activate data. CARFAX receives data from 100 thousand+ service shops through relationships we have built over decades, 1 shop at a time. We are increasingly using AI to automate and accelerate how we process that data. For example, AI has reduced the processing time for certain reports from 2 business days to less than 2 hours.

Our proprietary purpose built models decode nearly 180 categories of service and repair events with 99.5% accuracy. They extract far more data from our feeds than we could have a few years ago, and have helped our database reach 40 billion records this quarter. Refined over the years, these models cost a fraction of the general purpose alternatives. We are turning that rich data into better products and new insights. CARFAX Homegrown uses it to confidently identify vehicles sold and serviced by the same dealer throughout their lives. Our VIN level reliability forecast account for each car's unique history to show shoppers what a specific vehicle is likely to need and when.

This helps the CARFAX vehicle history report answer a key question. Is this a good car for me for the next 3 years? AI is also accelerating the development of new solutions. Built end to end with Gen-AI, Automotive Mastermind's marketing will launch 2 months early. And I will share more on that innovation shortly. Second, consumer engagement. Here, the same data advantage is creating new ways for consumers to find and engage with our information. CARFAX already has a strong digital presence. Generating more total and SEO traffic in the US than any other company in our competitive set. AI agents are now emerging as another channel. Organic traffic to CARFAX from LLMs remains small.

But grew double digits from the second quarter to the third. We have opened CARFAX to reputable agents and assistants as consumers are starting to use this channel. The early pattern is encouraging. When asked to find a used car most agents and shoppers to establish marketplaces and they will recommend checking the CARFAX. Unprompted. CARFAX listings is the only marketplace that provides a CARFAX report with every vehicle. And shoppers who start with an agent can ultimately reach a dealer through CARFAX. Traffic from agents is still minimal. But regardless of how people shop, a vehicle is often the second largest purchase of their lives.

As more vehicle shopping moves online, the demand for trusted independent information continues to grow. Across both innovation and consumer engagement, we are scaling AI within the governance framework we outlined in August. With clear safeguards for data, security, and human review. We Our second strategic priority is strengthening our market position by focusing on growth within our largest dealer groups. Expansion of CARFAX Homegrown and the launch of Automotive Mastermind's Marketing Lab. First, our largest dealer groups offer the clearest evidence of the value we deliver. These sophisticated ROI driven customers are adding CARFAX products across their dealerships. Service loyalty and listings are each growing at double digit rates among these groups. Reflecting the power of these solutions.

Second, homegrown is demonstrating impressive progress. Consumers see greater value in vehicles that have been sold and serviced by the same dealership throughout their life. And they trust CARFAX to verify that history. Dealers report that homegrown vehicles are sought after by consumers, sell faster and for more money, and they are driving new car sales. Returning as trade ins, these are some of the most economical vehicles for dealers to acquire, typically with lower reconditioning cost. Building on the success of our homegrown launch, we are extending homegrown across all CARFAX dealer and consumer assets. CARFAX listings so shoppers can find these vehicles, and to CarCare, so owners can see the value of continued service at the selling dealership.

And the dealer tools to help dealers grow their homegrown inventory. Third, marketing lab. Our newest innovation at Automotive Mastermind. Mastermind identifies customers most likely to buy and Marketing Lab, powered by our AI agent turns that insight into action. Dealers describe the customers they want to reach in plain language. And the agent builds the target audience personalizes the campaign, activates it across digital and traditional media, and tracks performance. By moving from informing dealer decisions to driving results, we continue to strengthen our market position. Our third strategic priority is creating 1 Mobility Global. Optimizing our structure to better capture the opportunity we see across the $8 trillion automotive market. Most of which is driven by consumer spending.

We support the consumer decision journey from the beginning to end. Our planning solution forecasts help OEMs and suppliers understand which vehicles consumers will want and buy in the future. Sales solution helps OEMs and dealers understand who is shopping, what they are shopping for, what they will pay, and what message will resonate. Throughout the ownership life cycle, CARFAX helps consumers decide. Which car to buy, how much to pay, to service it, and when to sell it. More than 60 million consumers have a direct relationship with us. And hundreds of millions visit our sites each year for information.

And while our businesses developed independently, together, they give us a view of the consumer, from the first forecast to the final trade in with each business making the others smarter. Our first product combining Automotive Mastermind and CARFAX will bring this opportunity to life. Automotive Mastermind identifies which consumers are likely to trade in or buy a new vehicle, and when. CARFAX CarCare uses the CARFAX platform to help 60 million vehicle owners maintain their vehicles. Starting next year, dealers subscribing to both products can combine these capabilities. Mastermind's offer already the most targeted in the industry, will reach participating dealers' customers through CarCare.

Backed by the trusted CarFax brand, dealers get a stronger response, owners receive timely relevant offers rather than generic ones, and both subscriptions become more valuable. Alongside this product development, we are completing our standalone foundation by moving to our own systems. We remain on track with the transition from S&P Global having already migrated hundreds of systems We expect to complete this effort within 18 months of the spin. This work lays the foundation to scale, innovate and unlock OneMobility Global's full growth potential. Let me close with a few final thoughts. Our mission remains at the heart of everything we do. Helping people buy, sell and own vehicles with more confidence.

Our unique combination of proprietary data, trusted brands and customer relationships reinforces my conviction in what we are building. This quarter's results validated what we said in August. The adjustments we made earlier this year were the right ones. We delivered on our commitments and believe we are well positioned to continue to build momentum into 2027. Heading into 2027, our priorities are clear. Sustain the momentum at CARFAX, deepen our relationships with OEMs, suppliers and dealers in B2B, continue expanding CARFAX internationally and finish the system work that lets us operate as 1 company. And underneath all of this is execution. Moving faster, putting AI to work across the business and building a foundation that scales.

1 quarter in, we recognize that we are just getting started, and significant work lies ahead. We are encouraged by our progress and energized by the future as 1 Mobility Global. With that, let me hand it over to Matthew.
